signals.signal: Erste Group's H1-2026 footprint appendix gives, at 30/06/2026: Czech Republic 4.6m customers / 9,175 FTE / 322 branches; Romania 3.0m / 4,909 / 294; Slovakia 1.9m / 3,471 / 128; Croatia 1.4m / 3,066 / 126; Hungary 1.2m / 3,434 / 97; Serbia 0.5m / 1,283 / 89; Poland 6.2m / 10,222 / 305; Austria 4.4m / 16,728 / 714. Group total: 23.2m customers, 55,231 FTE, 2,065 branches. Note the country boxes sum to 2,075, i.e. 10 more than the stated group total of 2,065 - a small unreconciled difference in Erste's own slide.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, H1 2026 investor/conference-call presentation (IR_Pres_CC_260730_H126.pdf), appendix 'Erste Group's geographic footprint', page 32
signals.implies: This is the first group-level branch denominator against which Printec can size country self-service estates. Branch count is the ceiling on in-branch cash automation (teller cash recyclers, assisted-service kiosks) and the floor under off-branch ATM/managed-services demand: 2,065 branches across 8 markets, of which only 714 are in high-cost Austria, means ~1,351 CEE branches are the addressable base for branch-format conversion, and each converted cash desk needs a recycler or deposit ATM.
signals.likelihood: Certain - already disclosed; the question is conversion pace, not whether
signals.followup: Reconcile the 10-branch gap by pulling each subsidiary's own H1-2026 report (Ceska sporitelna, Slovenska sporitelna, BCR, Erste Bank Hungary, Erste&Steiermarkische, Erste Bank Srbija); ask Erste IR whether the group figure excludes a category (e.g. self-service-only points or private-banking centres).

signals.signal: IT expenses rose to EUR 485 million in H1-2026 from EUR 344 million in H1-2025 (+41.0%), 'most importantly due to the inclusion of Poland (EUR 129 million)'. Stripping Poland out, underlying IT spend was ~EUR 356m, i.e. +3.5% yoy. Separately, integration costs of EUR 73 million were booked in H1-2026 and are guided at up to EUR 180 million gross for full-year 2026. Other administrative expenses EUR 1,075m (+33.1%), general administrative expenses EUR 3,537m (+30.7%), cost/income ratio 44.4% (from 47.7%).
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, Interim Report H1 2026, 'Earnings performance in brief'
signals.implies: Plain English: almost all of Erste's IT-cost growth this half is the Polish acquisition, not a new technology programme in the CEE core. That cuts two ways for Printec: (a) the CEE core banks are running flat IT budgets, so new spend has to be justified as cost-out - managed services and outsourced ATM operations sell better than capex refresh; (b) the EUR 180m 2026 integration envelope is genuinely new discretionary money concentrated in Poland.
signals.likelihood: High that the CEE-core flat-budget picture persists through 2027 given the sub-45% cost/income target
signals.followup: Get the Q3-2026 report (due ~end Oct 2026) to see whether IT expense ex-Poland stays ~flat; check whether Erste Group IT (the shared services entity, Erste Digital) is running any group ATM/self-service tender.

signals.signal: Erste closed the acquisition of a 49% controlling shareholding in Poland's third-largest bank and consolidated it from 09/01/2026. H1-2026 impact: EUR 59.3bn of the balance-sheet increase, EUR 41.4bn Polish loan portfolio, EUR 738m of general administrative expenses, EUR 129m of IT expenses, EUR 193m of amortisation/depreciation. Erste states the acquired brand 'will be fully written off following rebranding in 2026' (EUR 30m gross) and customer relationships will be amortised over ten years at ~EUR 210m p.a. Poland adds 6.2m customers, 10,222 FTE and 305 branches to the group.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, Interim Report H1 2026, 'Outlook' and 'Earnings performance in brief'; footprint appendix of the H1 2026 CC presentation
signals.implies: A full rebranding of a 305-branch, ~6.2m-customer Polish bank inside calendar 2026 is a hard-dated, fleet-wide re-livery and re-software event: ATM screen sets and topper branding, card re-issuance, POS terminal software/branding, branch signage and self-service furniture. Poland is outside Printec's 17-country footprint, but the group standards set in the EBP integration (ATM software stack, managed-services model, monitoring tooling) will be pushed down into the CEE subsidiaries afterwards - so this is the moment to get onto the group vendor list.
signals.likelihood: Rebrand is committed and dated to 2026; group-standard spillover into CEE is likely 2027-2028
signals.followup: Identify which ATM/self-service vendor EBP runs (the acquired bank's incumbent) and whether Erste is standardising the group on it; watch for a Polish rebrand tender notice and any group framework agreement for ATM managed services.

signals.entity: Erste Group Bank AG — 12-month branch trend by country
signals.signal: Branch counts from Erste's own footprint slide at three dates (30/06/2025 / 31/12/2025 / 30/06/2026): Slovakia 150 / 140 / 128 (-22, -14.7% yoy — the deepest cut in the group); Austria 737 / 732 / 714 (-23, -3.1%); Czech Republic 336 / 329 / 322 (-14, -4.2%); Croatia 128 / 128 / 126 (-2); Hungary 98 / 97 / 97 (-1); Serbia 88 / 88 / 89 (+1); Romania 298 / 290 / 294 (-4 yoy but +4 in H1-2026 — the only country ADDING branches); Poland 307 (31/12/2025) / 305. Group ex-Poland: 1,841 branches at 30/06/2025 falling to 1,760 at 30/06/2026, i.e. -81 branches / -4.4% in twelve months. FTE ex-Poland fell from 45,942 to 45,009 (-933, -2.0%). Czech FTE alone fell 9,629 to 9,175 (-454, -4.7%).
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, appendix 'Erste Group's geographic footprint' in the H1-2025 (01/08/2025), FY-2025 (26/02/2026) and H1-2026 (30/07/2026) conference-call presentations
signals.implies: Plain English: Erste is quietly shrinking its branch network everywhere except Romania and Serbia, and doing it fastest in Slovakia. Every closed branch has to have its cash volume absorbed somewhere, and Erste's own Croatian playbook (cashless branch + 24h self-service zone) shows the mechanism. That converts directly into demand for deposit-capable ATMs / recyclers, unattended self-service zones and the managed services to run them. Slovakia (-22 branches in a year, Slovenska sporitelna) is the single most under-covered opportunity this implies — no Printec signal file exists for it.
signals.likelihood: High — the trend is three consecutive reporting dates and is underpinned by a stated sub-45% cost/income target
signals.followup: OPEN A SLOVAKIA WORKSTREAM: pull Slovenska sporitelna's own branch/ATM locator and its H1-2026 report to get the ATM count and deposit-capable share behind the 128 branches; the group deck gives no ATM figures for any country. Also check the NBS (Narodna banka Slovenska) payment-statistics release for the Slovak ATM fleet.

signals.entity: Erste Group — reconciliation of group branch figures vs country locator pulls
signals.signal: Reconciling Erste's group disclosure at 30/06/2026 against the same-day locator pulls made by sibling country research this run (27/08/2026): Hungary matches exactly (group 97 branches vs Erste Bank Hungary's own GEM locator API 97). Romania: group 294 vs BCR's locator 282 branch records and BCR's own H1-2026 statement of '284 unitati retail' — a gap of ~10-12 explained by BCR's 19 business centres and 15 corporate mobile offices, which sit outside the retail locator. Croatia: group 126 vs Erste&Steiermarkische's /v1/branches endpoint 106 — a gap of 20, the largest proportional discrepancy. Separately, Erste's own H1-2026 slide does not internally reconcile: the eight country boxes sum to 2,075 branches against a stated group total of 2,065, whereas at 31/12/2025 the country boxes summed to exactly the stated 2,111.
signals.source_name: Erste Group H1-2026 CC presentation footprint appendix, cross-checked against Erste Bank Hungary, BCR and Erste&Steiermarkische public locator APIs
signals.implies: Practical rule for sizing Printec proposals: a bank's public branch locator is a reliable proxy for the RETAIL, cash-handling estate (Hungary matches to the unit), but understates the group figure by the corporate/business-centre tail. Use the locator number, not the IR number, when sizing teller-recycler or in-branch cash-automation deployments; use the IR number when sizing enterprise managed services. The Croatian 20-branch gap is worth resolving before quoting Erste Croatia.
signals.likelihood: Applies immediately to any Erste-subsidiary proposal
signals.followup: Ask Erste&Steiermarkische IR (or read its own H1-2026 Croatian statutory report on erstebank.hr) what the 20 non-locator branches are — likely corporate centres and Erste Card/leasing offices; confirm whether they hold cash.

signals.entity: Erste Group Bank AG — cost discipline
signals.signal: Operating expenses excluding Erste Bank Polska rose just +1.8% yoy and FELL -0.3% qoq in Q2-2026; total group opex was EUR 1,771m in Q2-2026 (+29.7% yoy including EBP). Erste's 2026 cost guidance of ~EUR 7bn (FX-adjusted) is stated as '~ +3%' excluding EBP, attributed to 'lower wage increases (compared to 2025) and efficiency gains'. Cost/income ratio improved to 44.4% (H1-2025: 47.7%) and the full-year target was tightened to 'less than 45%'. Q2-2026 Poland-specific costs inside the total: EUR 65m amortisation of customer stock and brand, plus EUR 43m integration costs, with no integration costs booked at parent-company level in Q2-2026.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Operating trends: operating expenses' (page 17) and 'Outlook' in the Interim Report H1 2026
signals.implies: A ~+3% ex-Poland cost ceiling and an explicit 'efficiency gains' commitment means capex-heavy ATM/self-service refresh proposals will struggle at Erste's CEE subsidiaries this cycle. The winning framing for Printec is opex-neutral or opex-negative: ATM managed services / outsourced estate operation, cash-cycle optimisation and cash-in-transit reduction through recyclers, and moving cash off manned counters. Sell against the branch-closure programme, not against a technology roadmap.
signals.likelihood: High — guidance is confirmed and the CIR target was tightened, not loosened
signals.followup: Model a cost-per-transaction comparison (manned teller vs recycler vs managed ATM) in EUR for a Slovak/Czech branch, so the Printec pitch lands inside Erste's own efficiency narrative. Re-check at Q3-2026 (due ~end Oct 2026) whether ex-EBP opex is still ~+3%.

signals.entity: Banca Comerciala Romana (BCR, Erste Group) — Romania segment
signals.signal: Romania was the ONLY Erste core segment where both the operating result and the cost/income ratio DETERIORATED in H1-2026. Erste attributes it to falling net interest income (lower market rates, higher deposit expense) while 'operating expenses rose mainly due to higher personnel, legal & consultancy costs as well as business operation costs'. Romanian banking tax more than doubled to EUR 39m (H1-2025: EUR 20m). At the same time BCR ADDED 4 branches in the quarter (290 at 31/03/2026 to 294 at 30/06/2026) while cutting 69 FTE (4,978 to 4,909).
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, Interim Report H1 2026, Romania segment commentary; footprint appendices of the Q1-2026 and H1-2026 CC presentations
signals.implies: BCR is the clearest cost-out target in the group: margins compressing, taxes rising, headcount falling, yet branches increasing. That combination is only sustainable if cash and routine transactions move to machines — which is precisely the gap BCR's own locator exposes (1,100 cash-dispense-only ATMs against 568 deposit-capable multifunction machines). Printec is already named on NCR Atleos's BCR reference page as the channel partner, so this is an incumbency-defence and upsell case, not a cold approach: recycler conversion of the 1,100 cash-out-only units, plus managed services to absorb the 69 lost FTE.
signals.likelihood: High — the pressure is disclosed and structural, not a one-off
signals.followup: Time a BCR approach to the 2027 budget cycle (Q4-2026). Quantify the 1,100-unit recycler conversion in RON and frame it against the EUR 39m banking-tax increase and the FTE reduction.

signals.entity: Erste Bank Srbija (Erste Bank Serbia Group)
signals.signal: Erste's Serbia segment saw operating expenses rise 'mainly due to higher IT DEPRECIATION and higher personnel costs', with net interest income declining on higher deposit rates; operating result decreased and the cost/income ratio worsened. A new resolution-fund contribution of EUR 4m was introduced in Serbia in 2026. Serbia is Erste's smallest core market: 0.5m customers, 1,283 FTE, 89 branches at 30/06/2026 (up from 88 at both 30/06/2025 and 31/12/2025), with only 6.0% retail loan share and 5.5% retail deposit share.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, Interim Report H1 2026, Serbia segment commentary; H1-2026 CC presentation footprint appendix
signals.implies: 'Higher IT depreciation' means Erste Serbia has recently CAPITALISED a significant technology investment that is now hitting the P&L — a platform build is already sunk, which lowers appetite for new core-system spend but raises appetite for anything that monetises the platform (self-service channels, transaction monitoring, onboarding). With 89 branches and a 6% loan share, Erste Serbia is a challenger that has to acquire customers digitally and serve them cheaply: digital onboarding/eKYC and shared/managed ATM access are the fit, not a large owned fleet. Cross-reference the NBS Q1-2026 count of 3,336 ATMs / 187,957 POS for Serbia.
signals.likelihood: Medium — small unit, but the disclosed cost deterioration creates a 2027 budget conversation
signals.followup: Identify WHAT the capitalised Serbian IT asset is (check Erste Bank a.d. Novi Sad's own Serbian-language annual/interim report and NBS filings) — if it is a new core or digital-channel platform, the integration surface for Printec eKYC/monitoring is defined by it.

signals.signal: More than 11.8 million users have been onboarded to George, Erste's retail digital banking platform, across all core markets EXCEPT Poland. Overall digital sales share, applying straight-through-process criteria, reached 73%. George Invest (fully digital investment product) is live in Austria, Czechia and Slovakia only, and attracts customers with an average age of 35; the stock of securities savings plans reached 2.2m contracts. On the corporate side, the George business roll-out reached ~85,000 clients onboarded, up 12% year-to-date.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, H1 2026 conference-call presentation, retail and corporate operating-trends slides
signals.implies: Two openings. (1) 73% straight-through digital sales means the remaining 27% is assisted or branch-bound — the residual is dominated by identity-verification-heavy products, which is exactly where digital onboarding/eKYC and remote identification sell. (2) George is explicitly NOT yet in Poland (6.2m customers) and George Invest is only in 3 of 8 markets — the roll-out backlog is a multi-year integration programme with recurring onboarding/AML/monitoring workstreams. The 85,000-client corporate George base is small enough that business-onboarding and KYB tooling is still greenfield.
signals.likelihood: High — George extension to Poland is implied by the stated systems-integration next step
signals.followup: Establish which eKYC/identity vendor George currently uses per market (Erste Digital is the group IT entity); check whether the George-to-Poland roll-out is tendered separately or built in-house.

signals.signal: Erste's H1-2026 press conference deck states the Polish rebranding has already been executed and reports brand-recognition tracking 'after about 2.5 months, per 19 July 2026': 78% prompted and 28% spontaneous recognition among the Polish population, employer recommendation +6pp, overall satisfaction and loyalty +2pp, and 306,000 new retail customers since the beginning of the year. The deck lists 'Poland: Next steps' as exactly three items: Rebranding, SYSTEMS INTEGRATION, and increasing brand visibility. Integration costs of EUR 73m were booked in H1-2026 against a full-year 2026 guide of up to EUR 180m gross, plus EUR 240m of 2026 intangibles amortisation for customer stock and brand.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, H1 2026 press-conference presentation 'Central Europe: from following to shaping' (Bosek/Doerfler/Habeler-Drabek), slides 'Rebranding Poland' and 'Poland: Next steps'
signals.implies: 'Systems integration' is now the named forward workstream for a 305-branch, 6.2m-customer, 10,222-FTE bank, with roughly EUR 107m of the EUR 180m integration budget still unspent at 30/06/2026. Poland sits outside Printec's 17-country footprint, so the direct revenue is not addressable — but the group technology standards chosen in this integration (ATM software stack, self-service platform, monitoring, managed-services model) are what Erste will subsequently impose on the CEE subsidiaries that ARE Printec territory. Getting visibility of the EBP integration architecture in 2026 is the cheapest way to be pre-qualified for the CEE roll-out in 2027-2028.
signals.likelihood: Systems integration is committed and funded; CEE standardisation spillover likely 2027-2028
signals.followup: Watch Erste Digital (the group IT subsidiary) and EBP procurement notices for the integration's channel/self-service lots; confirm which ATM vendor EBP's ~305-branch estate runs today.

signals.signal: Hungary carries the heaviest transaction-related tax load in the group. Erste booked a Hungarian FINANCIAL TRANSACTION TAX of EUR 68m in H1-2026 (H1-2025: EUR 61m) and banking tax of EUR 121m for the full year 2026 (total Hungarian levies EUR 189m vs EUR 109m), including a windfall profit tax of EUR 98m (EUR 28m). Despite this, the Hungary segment grew net interest income and net fee income (higher payment fees) and improved its cost/income ratio, on a base of only 97 branches and 3,434 FTE serving 1.2m customers. Sibling research pulled Erste Bank Hungary's own locator API the same run: 505 ATMs across 276 settlements, of which 268 (53%) are cash-deposit capable — the highest deposit-ready share of the major Hungarian banks — leaving 237 cash-out-only machines.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, Interim Report H1 2026, Hungary segment commentary; Erste Bank Hungary locator API (erstebank.hu/bin/erstegroup/gemesgapi/locations)
signals.implies: A per-transaction tax makes every payment message a costed event, which puts a hard commercial premium on accurate transaction categorisation, reporting and reconciliation — a transaction-monitoring/reporting sale rather than a pure AML one. Separately, 505 ATMs against just 97 branches is the group's most machine-dependent retail model: the network IS the branch estate, so 237 cash-out-only units are a well-defined recycler upgrade target, and the thin branch base makes third-party managed services structurally attractive.
signals.likelihood: Levies are legislated for 2026; the ATM upgrade decision is a 2027 budget item
signals.followup: Confirm from Erste Bank Hungary's own Hungarian-language H1-2026 report whether the 505 ATMs are self-operated or already outsourced, and whether it participates in any Hungarian shared-ATM arrangement.

signals.entity: Erste Group Bank AG — 2030 medium-term ambition
signals.signal: Alongside H1-2026 results Erste defined its first medium-term financial ambition to 2030: double earnings per share from an adjusted 2025 baseline of EUR 7.72 (reported EUR 8.24) to more than EUR 15 by 2030, an EPS CAGR of ~15%, with return on tangible equity above 20% throughout the forecast period. The four stated drivers are sustainable organic growth in lending/deposits/asset management, 'INORGANIC OPTIONALITY IN POLAND AND ACROSS CENTRAL EUROPE', better operating efficiency driven by larger scale, and a continued benign credit environment. 2026 guidance was upgraded: net profit above EUR 4bn, loans ~EUR 290bn, fees ~EUR 4bn, opex ~EUR 7bn FX-adjusted, cost/income below 45%.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Financial outlook to 2030: definition of medium-term financial ambition' (page 29-30); H1 2026 results press release
signals.implies: Erste has publicly committed to further acquisitions in Central Europe — Printec's own territory — and to 'efficiency driven by larger scale'. Each CEE bank acquisition triggers exactly the integration work Printec sells into: estate consolidation and rationalisation of duplicate ATM fleets, terminal and card re-branding, merging of AML/transaction-monitoring stacks, HSM and key migration, and a managed-services contract to run the combined estate. Printec should maintain a live watchlist of plausible Erste targets in CZ/SK/HU/HR/RS/RO and be positioned as the integration partner before a deal is announced, not after.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high that at least one further Central European acquisition is announced within the 6-12 month window, given the explicit statement and the 15.2% CET1 ratio
signals.followup: Build the target watchlist: mid-sized CEE banks with sub-scale branch/ATM estates in Erste's eight core markets plus adjacent ones. Track Erste's CET1 rebuild (15.2% at 30/06/2026 after the 455bp EBP hit) as the timing indicator — a return towards 16-17% is the practical precondition for the next deal.

signals.signal: Erste booked a gain of EUR 116 million on the sale of a Croatian subsidiary (Erste Card Club, the Diners Club Croatia card business) in H1-2026, and states Croatian net fee and commission income FELL 'mainly on lower payment fees due to the sale of Erste Card Club'. Croatia otherwise grew net interest income and improved its cost/income ratio, with operating expenses 'by and large stable'. Erste Croatia at 30/06/2026: 1.4m customers, 3,066 FTE, 126 branches (from 128 at both 30/06/2025 and 31/12/2025), 16.3% retail loan share, 14.7% retail deposit share.
signals.source_name: Erste Group Bank AG, Interim Report H1 2026, Croatia segment commentary and 'Earnings performance in brief'
signals.implies: Erste has permanently exited Croatian card issuing and acquiring, so its Croatian fee engine now leans harder on account and cash services — which raises the strategic weight of the self-service estate at exactly the moment Croatia legislates a statutory cash-access right effective 01/01/2027. Sibling research this run found Erste Croatia running 665 ATMs of which only 199 (29.9%) accept deposits, and 106 branches of which 100 still carry a manned cash desk. A bank with no card business, a stable cost base and a 2027 cash-access deadline is a recycler and managed-services buyer, and the freed EUR 116m gain is unallocated capital.
signals.likelihood: High — the 01/01/2027 statutory cash-access right is a dated trigger nine months into the forward window
signals.followup: Track the Croatian shared national ATM network negotiation (HNB / Croatian Banking Association) — if Erste joins a pooled network its own 665-unit fleet becomes a consolidation and outsourcing candidate rather than an upgrade candidate; the two outcomes need different Printec propositions.

coverage_notes: PRIMARY-SOURCE-ONLY RUN. This unit was NEVER REACHED in the 30/07/2026 run, so everything here is new ground rather than re-verification. Angles used, all novel entry points relative to the baseline: (1) enumerated Erste's CDN asset directory (cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/.../Investor_Relations/<year>/...) directly off the financial-reports page rather than using the JS report picker, which exposed stable, permanent PDF URLs for every 2026 document; (2) downloaded and locally text-extracted (pdfminer) FOUR primary PDFs: the H1-2026 Interim Report, the H1-2026 conference-call deck, the H1-2026 PRESS-CONFERENCE deck (a distinct document most coverage ignores, and the only source for the Poland rebranding tracker), and the H1-2026 results press release; (3) built a genuine 12-month TIME SERIES by pulling the same footprint appendix from three vintages (H1-2025 deck 01/08/2025, FY-2025 deck 26/02/2026, H1-2026 deck 30/07/2026) — this is what turns a static branch count into the branch-closure trend that is the core deliverable; (4) reconciled the group figures against the same-day (27/08/2026) locator-API pulls made by the sibling Hungary, Romania and Croatia agents, which is the country-vs-group reconciliation the brief asked for and which no previous run had ever done. VALIDATION OF METHOD: the FY-2025 country boxes sum exactly to the stated group total of 2,111 branches, which confirms the country-to-value mapping recovered from the PDF text layer; the H1-2026 boxes sum to 2,075 against a stated 2,065, and that 10-branch discrepancy is reported as an observed inconsistency in Erste's own slide rather than resolved. GENUINE GAPS: (a) Erste discloses NO ATM, self-service, POS or terminal counts at group level in any H1-2026 document — every machine figure in these signals comes from a subsidiary locator API, not from Erste; (b) Erste's own newsroom/press-release listing is JavaScript-rendered and returned no article links to a plain fetch, so the Aug-2026 non-IR news sweep and the German-language press angle are NOT covered — this is the largest gap in this file; (c) no subsidiary-level primary disclosure was opened for SLOVAKIA (Slovenska sporitelna) or CZECHIA (Ceska sporitelna), and Slovakia is the group's fastest-shrinking network (-22 branches yoy) with no Printec signal file anywhere in this run — it is the single highest-value follow-up; (d) no Capital Markets Day material exists for this window; the 2030 ambition was published with the H1 results, not at a separate CMD; (e) Austria's retail market shares are shown on the slide as 22.4%/24.7% but the slide footnote says Austrian market shares are 'not yet available as of 30/06/2026', so they are deliberately NOT cited as a claim here.
access_issues: (1) BLOCKING CONSTRAINT: this session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by sibling agents before this agent issued its first query, so ZERO web searches were possible. All research was done by constructing and fetching primary URLs directly with curl + a desktop User-Agent, and extracting PDFs locally with pdfminer. No aggregator or press source was used or needed. (2) https://www.erstegroup.com/en/investors/reports/presentations returns HTTP 404 — the presentations index no longer exists as a standalone page; presentations are served from the financial-reports page. Route used instead: parsed the CDN PDF hrefs out of https://www.erstegroup.com/en/investors/reports/financial-reports (HTTP 200, 1.07MB). (3) https://www.erstegroup.com/de/presse/pressemitteilungen returns HTTP 404 (German press index moved or renamed). (4) https://www.erstegroup.com/en/news-media/press-releases returns HTTP 200 but the article list is rendered client-side via the /bin/erstegroup/gemesgapi endpoints; a plain fetch yields the page shell with no article links, and the desktop-UA retry did not change this. The documented escalation to Claude-in-Chrome was NOT attempted because the session's remaining budget was better spent extracting the four primary PDFs; this is logged, not silently dropped. (5) All four PDF downloads succeeded on first attempt at full size (interim report 1.71MB, CC deck 1.21MB, press-conference deck 12.6MB, press release 80KB); note the press-conference deck is image-heavy and yielded only ~6.6k characters of text layer, so its charts are not machine-readable — figures taken from it are limited to those present as real text.
operator_requests: Nothing is paywalled — but two operator actions would materially close the gaps above. (1) Run a browser-rendered (Claude-in-Chrome or equivalent) pass over https://www.erstegroup.com/en/news-media/press-releases and the German equivalent for the 01/07/2026-27/08/2026 window; the list is JS-only and no non-IR Erste news could be captured this run. (2) SPAWN A DEDICATED SLOVAKIA / SLOVENSKA SPORITELNA AGENT for the next run. Erste cut Slovak branches from 150 to 128 in twelve months — the deepest network reduction anywhere in the group — and there is no Slovak file in this run's parts directory at all. Needed: Slovenska sporitelna's own branch/ATM locator feed, its H1-2026 report, and the NBS (Narodna banka Slovenska) payment-statistics release for the national ATM/POS fleet. (3) Lower priority: the H1-2026 press-conference deck (IR_Pres_PC_260730_H126.pdf, 12.6MB) is image-heavy and would repay OCR — its Poland integration and Central-Europe-infrastructure slides are largely graphics that the text layer does not carry.
